findings.title: Include the identity type in denial cache keys
findings.body: The denial key uses only the parsed subject ID, discarding IdentityType. Supported subjects such as `anonymous:0` and `render:0` therefore share a key for the same namespace, action, name and folder. If an anonymous dashboard read is denied, a subsequent renderer read hits that denial and returns false without evaluating the renderer's unconditional dashboard-read permission. Include the identity type (or full typed subject) in the key so one principal cannot poison another principal's authorization result.

findings.title: Encode denial cache key components unambiguously
findings.body: Concatenating the resource name and parent folder with underscores creates collisions for valid UIDs containing underscores. For the same namespace, user and action, a request for name `a_b` in folder `c` produces the same key as name `a` in folder `b_c`. A denial for the first request consequently denies the second request for 30 seconds, even if the user has direct or inherited permission on it. Use an unambiguous encoding, such as a serialized tuple or length-prefixed components, for the denial key.
